reasoning: The plastic doll is classified in heading 9503 (not a textile product under 102.21). For marking of goods from Mexico under 19 CFR 102.11/102.20, both the finished doll and its dedicated molded parts fall in heading 9503, so simple assembly by screwing and gluing in Mexico fails the tariff shift and is excluded by 19 CFR 102.17. Under 102.11(c) and substantial transformation (analogous to N331459), all plastic parts impart the essential character and are molded in China.

decisive_step: Weaving the shower curtain fabric in China (and shifting the rug materials to heading 5703 in Cambodia, though for the curtain/primary textile good it is fabric formation in China)
flip: Weave the polyester shower curtain fabric in Cambodia (and tuft the rug fabric in Cambodia).
reasoning: For the textile components under 19 CFR 102.21(c)(2): the shower curtain (heading 6303) originates where its fabric is formed by a fabric-making process, which is China. For the tufted bath rug (heading 5703), under (c)(2) and 102.21(e), a change to heading 5703 from any other chapter occurs in Cambodia where the tufted fabric (heading 5802) is backed with TPR, cut, and bound into a carpet (or under (c)(4) as in N336924, tufting in China is the most important process). Either way, the primary textile component (shower curtain) originates in China.

decisive_step: knitting of the plush and faux shearling fabrics in Vietnam
flip: Forming the plush fabric or the faux shearling fabric in China instead of Vietnam.
reasoning: The blankets are classified under heading 6301, HTSUS. Because manufacturing occurs in Vietnam and China, 19 CFR 102.21(c)(1) does not apply. Under 19 CFR 102.21(c)(2) and the tariff shift rule in 102.21(e)(1) for headings 6301-6306, origin is conferred by the single country where the fabric comprising the good was formed by a fabric-making process. Following N348858 and N348569 (Scenario 1), since all fabrics for both styles are knit in Vietnam, Vietnam is the country of origin.

decisive_step: Weaving of the polyester shell fabrics in China
flip: Weaving the front or back polyester fabric in Vietnam (or dyeing, printing, and performing two qualifying finishing operations on the fabrics in Vietnam if classified under 9404.90.95) would shift origin to Vietnam.
reasoning: Decorative pillows are classified under subheading 9404.90, HTSUS. Because the product involves two countries, 19 CFR 102.21(c)(1) does not apply. Under 19 CFR 102.21(c)(2) and (e)(1) (and (e)(2)(ii) if applicable, as the fabrics were not both dyed and printed with two qualifying finishing operations), origin is conferred by the single country where the fabrics comprising the good were formed by a fabric-making process (see N345210). Since all shell and piping fabrics are woven in China, the country of origin is China.

key_factors: (c)(5) last country of important assembly or manufacturing process
decisive_step: Weaving the back and lining fabrics, cutting, sewing, and stuffing the pillow in Vietnam
flip: Weave the mink velvet back fabric and nonwoven lining in China so all shell fabrics are formed in China, shifting origin to China under (c)(2)
reasoning: The decorative pillow is classified under subheading 9404.90 (not made of cotton, so 102.21(e)(2) does not apply). Under 102.21(c)(1), it is not wholly produced in one country. Under (c)(2), the tariff shift rule for 9404.90 requires fabric formation in a single country, which fails as the face fabric is woven in China and the back/lining fabrics are formed in Vietnam. Subheading 9404.90 is excluded from (c)(3)(ii). Following N350421 and N351508, neither fabric is more important under (c)(4), so origin defaults under (c)(5) to Vietnam, the last country of important manufacturing/assembly.

decisive_step: Manufacturing of the carbonless paper coated with microcapsules and resin-based developers in Germany
flip: Manufacturing the carbonless copy paper in Mexico instead of Germany
reasoning: The finished good is self-copy (carbonless) paper of heading 4809 or 4816. In Mexico, German-origin carbonless paper (already of heading 4809) is merely layered with Mexican bond paper (heading 4810), rewound, and slit/cut into smaller rolls or sheets. Under 19 CFR 102.11(a)(3)/102.20, the German carbonless paper does not undergo the required tariff shift. Under 102.11(b)(1) and substantial transformation principles, the carbonless paper imparts the essential character to the self-copy paper, conferring German origin.

key_factors: (c)(5) last country of important assembly or manufacturing process
decisive_step: Weaving the back fabric and cutting, sewing, and stuffing the pillow in Vietnam
flip: Weaving the velvet back fabric in China instead of Vietnam so all shell fabrics are formed in China under (c)(2)
reasoning: The decorative pillow is classified under subheading 9404.90.20, HTSUS. Under 19 CFR 102.21(c)(1), it is not wholly obtained in a single country. Under (c)(2) and 102.21(e)(1) for 9404.90, origin is where the fabric comprising the good was formed; since the face fabric is woven in China and the back fabric in Vietnam, no single country forms the fabric. Subheading 9404.90 is excluded from (c)(3). Under (c)(4), neither fabric formation yields a single most important process. Under (c)(5), consistent with N345364, origin is Vietnam, where the back fabric is woven and the pillow is assembled.

decisive_step: Fabrication of the thermocouple subassembly by laser welding and final assembly of the RF probe in Mexico
flip: If the thermocouple subassembly and RF probe were fabricated and assembled in the United States or South Korea, and only packaged or fitted with a protective sheath in Mexico.
reasoning: In Mexico, raw stainless steel hypo-tubes (US/South Korea), constantan wire (US), cable (US/China), and connectors (Hungary) undergo tinning, ultrasonic washing, laser welding to form the thermocouple dome, handle molding, and soldering into a finished medical RF probe of heading 9018. Under the part 102 tariff shift rules (and substantial transformation principles as in N330771 and N349989), all foreign materials undergo the required tariff shift and lose their separate identities in Mexico, conferring Mexican origin.

key_factors: (c)(5) last country of important assembly or manufacturing process
decisive_step: Weaving of back fabric, forming of nonwoven lining, and assembly/stuffing in Vietnam
flip: Weave the mink velvet back fabric and form the nonwoven lining in China instead of Vietnam
reasoning: Following identical precedent N356882, the pillow of subheading 9404.90 is not wholly obtained under (c)(1). Because shell fabrics are formed in both China (face fabric) and Vietnam (back fabric and lining), no single country forms the fabric under (c)(2). Subheading 9404.90 is excluded from (c)(3). Under (c)(4), neither country's fabric formation is more important. Therefore, under 19 CFR 102.21(c)(5), origin is conferred by the last country where an important manufacturing and assembly process occurred, which is Vietnam.

decisive_step: Knitting of the microfiber pile fabric in China
flip: Knit the microfiber pile fabric in Cambodia instead of China
reasoning: The microfiber cleaning cloth is classified under subheading 6307.10, HTSUS (or 6307.90). Under 19 CFR 102.21(c)(1), the good is not wholly obtained in a single country. Under 19 CFR 102.21(c)(2) and 102.21(e), the tariff shift rule for heading 6307.10 (and 6307.90) confers origin on the single country where the fabric comprising the good was formed by a fabric-making process. Following N353787 and N350428, because the knit pile fabric is formed in China, the country of origin is China.

decisive_step: Cutting and sewing the fabric panels into finished bibs in India
flip: Forming the bibs from a single layer of fabric without assembling two or more component parts, which would shift origin to Uzbekistan where the fabric was woven
reasoning: Woven cotton baby bibs are classified as babies' clothing accessories under heading 6209, HTSUS (unlike the made-up articles in companion ruling N356395). Because the bibs are produced in both Uzbekistan and India, 19 CFR 102.21(c)(1) does not apply. Under 102.21(c)(2) and the tariff shift rule for heading 6209 in 102.21(e)(1) for goods consisting of two or more component parts, origin is conferred where the two fabric layers are cut and wholly assembled into finished bibs, which is India.

decisive_step: Weaving of the polyester slub and velvet shell fabrics in China
flip: Forming either the front or back shell fabric in Vietnam instead of China
reasoning: Under 19 CFR 102.21(c)(2) and 102.21(e)(1), the origin of a decorative pillow classifiable under subheading 9404.90.20, HTSUS (which is not listed in the 102.21(e)(2) exceptions), is the single country where the fabric comprising the good was formed by a fabric-making process. Following N356883 and N345210, the piping, labels, thread, and fiberfill are disregarded for tariff shift purposes, and the front and back shell fabrics are both woven in China. Thus, origin is China.

key_factors: (c)(4) most important assembly or manufacturing process
decisive_step: tufting chenille yarns into primary backing fabrics in China
flip: Perform the tufting of the chenille yarns into the primary backing fabrics in Vietnam
reasoning: Classified in heading 5703 (tufted bath mat). (c)(1) fails as processing occurs in two countries. (c)(2) fails because the tufted fabric is already classified in Chapter 57 when exported from China to Vietnam, so not all foreign materials shift from another chapter in a single country. (c)(3) fails as assembly is split between tufting in China and laminating/sewing in Vietnam. Under (c)(4), following N336924, tufting the chenille pile into the base fabric is the most important manufacturing process, conferring China origin.

decisive_step: Lamination and coating of the aluminum foil with backing materials in Canada
flip: Using backed aluminum foil of heading 7607 imported into Canada rather than unbacked foil or shifting the lamination process outside Canada
reasoning: Under Amcor Flexibles v. US, all four multilayer packaging products are classified in heading 7607 (backed aluminum foil, 7607.20) because the foil provides the functional barrier while paper, plastics, and wax serve as backing. For goods of Canada (Atlantic Coated Papers), Part 102 marking rules apply (see N333961, N337651). Under 19 CFR 102.20, laminating/backing foil effects the required tariff shift to subheading 7607.20 and constitutes a substantial transformation in Canada, conferring Canadian origin.

decisive_step: Weaving the yarn into narrow woven ribbon in China
flip: Both dyeing and printing the greige ribbon in the United Kingdom accompanied by two or more qualifying finishing operations (e.g., bleaching, shrinking, permanent stiffening)
reasoning: The narrow woven ribbon (heading 5806) is produced in multiple countries, so (c)(1) does not apply. Under 19 CFR 102.21(c)(2) and (e)(1) for heading 5806, dyeing and finishing alone in the UK do not satisfy the first tariff shift rule (which requires both dyeing and printing plus two qualifying finishing operations). Under the second rule, a shift to heading 5806 from yarn by a fabric-making process (weaving) occurs in China, conferring Chinese origin.

decisive_step: formation of the polyester woven fabric in China
flip: Form the woven fabric in Cambodia, or both print and dye the fabric in Cambodia with at least two required finishing operations.
reasoning: Woven scarves/sarongs are classified in heading 6214, HTSUS. Under 19 CFR 102.21(c)(1), the good is not wholly obtained in a single country. Under 102.21(c)(2) and 102.21(e)(1), the tariff shift rule for heading 6214 requires a shift from yarn/fiber, or from fabric via dyeing AND printing plus two finishing operations. Because the fabric was only printed, cut, and sewn in Cambodia, the rule defaults to the country where the fabric was formed by a fabric-making process, which is China.
